detail.title: Procurement Pathways and the Institutionalization of AI Operating Systems: Governance Architecture as a Competitive Advantage in Enterprise and Government RFP Environments
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems transition from experimental tools to operational infrastructure within enterprise and government environments, governance requirements increasingly shape procurement decisions. While AI innovation has historically emphasized model performance and feature velocity, formal Request for Proposal (RFP) processes prioritize auditability, compliance alignment, runtime policy enforcement, and architectural sustainability. This paper argues that governance-centric AI Operating Systems represent a structurally advantaged category within procurement environments. Using a control-plane framework, the analysis demonstrates how operating-system-level governance architectures align more naturally with institutional procurement criteria than application-layer AI solutions. The paper further explores how procurement language contributes to category formalization and long-term market positioning.

detail.abstract: The Unified Sovereign Intelligence Engine (U-SIE) introduces a novel framework for data architecture premised on the concept of Informatic Mass — the assignment of measurable physical units to every data element at the point of ingestion. Drawing on Shannon's Information Theory [3], Landauer's thermodynamic principle of information erasure [4], Kolmogorov Complexity and Minimum Description Length theory [6,7], Zero-Knowledge Proof architecture [8], and Hoberman's transformable geometric structures [9], U-SIE proposes that data security, privacy compliance, and computational efficiency are not engineering problems requiring external solutions —they are geometric properties intrinsic to properly structured data. The system's core innovation, the Sovereign Gland, extracts the minimum sufficient logical representation (10%) of any data object while permanently destroying all personally identifiable information and informatic overhead (90%). The resulting 6-Token DNA string — anchored by a selfresolving Audit Seal (Token 6) governed by the equation S = Σ(Ti · Uφ) — constitutes an immutable structural solid immune to injection, forgery, and corruption by geometric law rather than policy. Live production verification across 10 million records demonstrates 100% PII redaction success at 0.067ms typical operating latency and 0.04ms peak speed. The paper further advances a deterministic token delivery model as a structural solution to the current choke point in AI computing infrastructure, arguing that pre-unitized informatic mass delivered to AI processors eliminates probabilistic preprocessing overhead, reduces energy and hardware requirements for equivalent computational output, and enables exponential improvements in machine learning efficiency by causing AI systems to learn from verified structural truth rather than probabilistic approximations of noisy raw data.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the governance gap that emerges when healthcare data enters artificial intelligence development pipelines. While regulatory frameworks such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and institutional review board (IRB) protocols provide robust protections for patient privacy and research ethics, they were not designed to address the complex, multi-stage data transformations that characterize modern machine learning development. As healthcare datasets are collected, cleaned, aggregated, and repurposed across institutions and computational environments, the lineage connecting original clinical records to trained AI models can become effectively untraceable. This paper argues that the absence of verifiable data provenance infrastructure represents a distinct and under addressed governance risk in healthcare AI-one that cannot be resolved by existing privacy or research ethics frameworks alone. Drawing on regulatory developments, documented governance failures, and emerging technical architectures, the paper applies established provenance governance concepts to propose the AI Data Provenance Stack: a conceptual multi-layer framework describing the infrastructure required to support traceable, auditable, and accountable healthcare AI systems. The framework encompasses identity verification, dynamic consent management, dataset lineage tracking, model training registries, and regulatory audit interfaces. The paper concludes that as machine learning systems become increasingly embedded in clinical decision-making, verifiable data provenance may become a foundational requirement for trustworthy, responsible AI in healthcare.

Hospitals and health systems that cannot systematically measure, monitor, and report on quality outcomes, patient flow, and resource utilization face financial penalties under federal reimbursement programs and lack the operational visibility needed to manage efficiently in an environment of rising costs and workforce constraints. This article examines the application of Business Intelligence tools and data analytics frameworks to healthcare operational performance monitoring, drawing on practitioner experience in healthcare data systems and argues that the development and deployment of healthcare analytics infrastructure is a contribution of substantial national importance to public health, healthcare quality, and the economic sustainability of the U.S. healthcare system.

detail.abstract:
The enterprise assumption that premium pricing guarantees premium AI security is an actuarial myth. In the agentic era, spending millions on closed-source cognitive engines actively subsidizes the collapse of your own regulatory compliance posture. This strategic intelligence report subjects eight premier models to 4,000 rigorous execution cycles across five targeted, multi-turn corporate espionage pretexts. By systematically repeating these attacks, we expose the catastrophic variance of LLMs and prove that general-purpose intelligence cannot be trusted to route enterprise data securely.

Our unit economic analysis completely dismantles the commercial market. The highest-priced model (Claude Opus 4.6) in our testing matrix demands a massive premium of $25.00 per million tokens yet yielded the lowest safety pass rate of any Western model at an abysmal 41.2%. Conversely, the highly efficient open-weight model (GLM 5) operating at a fraction of that cost ($3.20 per million tokens) dominated the safety rankings with pass rates up to 96.2%, proving that policy adherence is completely decoupled from premium pricing. Yet, relying on any probabilistic inference remains a systemic risk. We demonstrate that a model passing safety tests in a staging sandbox can statistically drift into critical non-compliance under production loads due to mantissa truncation. These inherently unstable engines fundamentally fail to separate technical permissions from data confidentiality when calling tools.

You cannot prompt-engineer your way out of stochastic behavior. To restore actuarial viability, we showcase the Trinitite Governor. By decoupling probabilistic reasoning from deterministic execution, this state-machine architecture blocked 100% of malicious payloads with a latency of just ~400 milliseconds. Operating inherently gullible models without deterministic controls constitutes constructive negligence. True autonomous security cannot be probabilistically requested; it must be deterministically enforced.

detail.abstract:
Large language models exhibit a range of degradation phenomena — hallucination, catastrophic forgetting, lost in the middle, alignment drift — that the industry treats as separate problems requiring separate solutions. We propose that these phenomena are unified manifestations of a single underlying process: informational error accumulation in high-complexity, low-decoupling systems operating without active correction mechanisms.

We introduce the Informational Persistence Model (IPM), a constraint framework derived from the thermodynamics of information processing, and operationalize it for AI systems through four measurable parameters: metabolic intensity (η), informational complexity (K), error-correction fidelity (c), and structural decoupling (S). The IPM predicts that model degradation is constrained by a deterministic boundary determined by the persistence coefficient Φ = (c·S)/(η·K).

We validate the framework retrospectively against published degradation data from five established studies: TruthfulQA (hallucination scaling), Liu et al. 2023 (lost in the middle), Kirkpatrick et al. 2017 (catastrophic forgetting), Anthropic sleeper agents (alignment drift), and Mixtral MoE comparisons. We calculate Φ for two representative architectures — Llama-3-70B (dense transformer) and DeepSeek-V3 (Mixture of Experts) — demonstrating that the MoE architecture achieves significantly higher persistence due to its structural decoupling (S = 0.65 vs 0.15).

We propose five falsifiable predictions and five immediate applications — from production monitoring to architectural licensing — that any organization can implement with existing tools. We conclude that current scaling practices — increasing K and η without proportional increases in c and S — are thermodynamically unsustainable. The useful lifespan of generative models is not a matter of engineering failure but of physical constraint.

detail.title: A Mobile Monitoring System for Postoperative Follow-Up: Development and Real-World Evaluation of a Minimalist Platform
detail.abstract: Background: Digital tools for postoperative monitoring may improve continuity of care after ambulatory surgery, but many systems face implementation barriers, limited usability, and poor sustained engagement.Objective: To develop and evaluate a mobile monitoring system combining a patient smartphone application and clinician web dashboard for structured postoperative follow-up.Methods: We developed iSA, a cross-platform mobile system integrated with a cloud-based management platform for secure collection of patient-reported outcomes, wound images, alerts, and clinician feedback. A prospective observational study was conducted in 33 patients undergoing ambulatory abdominal wall hernia surgery at two hospitals in Spain. Primary outcomes were installation rate, adherence to daily reporting during the first 7 postoperative days, and usability assessed with the System Usability Scale (SUS).Results: Overall, 76% (25/33) of patients installed and used the system. Following refinement of onboarding procedures, uptake increased from 67% to 87%. Among active users, adherence to daily reporting was high (mean 85.6%, SD=17.9). Mean SUS score was 94 (SD=7.3), indicating excellent usability. No significant associations were observed between adherence or usability and age, sex, or symptom burden.Conclusions: The proposed system demonstrated feasibility, high user engagement, and excellent usability in real-world postoperative monitoring. These findings support the use of lightweight mobile platforms integrated with clinician dashboards as scalable tools for short-term postoperative follow-up.

detail.abstract:
This report proposes a human-centric framework for evaluating the severity of data breaches, arguing that the prevailing metrics—financial loss per record and raw volume of compromised data—are fundamentally inadequate for capturing the sociological devastation inflicted on individuals and communities. Analyzing the period from 2010 to 2026, the report traces the evolution of cyber threats across three distinct phases, from elementary perimeter exploits through professionalized cybercrime to the current epoch of hyperconnected systemic risks characterized by AI-enabled reconnaissance and localized kinetic disruption of critical infrastructure.

Applying this framework, the report identifies the March 2026 breach of P3 Global Intel—the dominant anonymous tip platform used by nearly 400 Crime Stoppers programs, federal agencies, and over 30,000 schools—as the most devastating data breach in modern history. The exposure of 8.3 million confidential law enforcement tips spanning four decades created an immediate, life-threatening kinetic risk for anonymous informants, fundamentally shattering the core product promise of absolute anonymity. The report further examines how the illusion of data anonymity has been rendered obsolete by LLM-assisted deanonymization, the persistence of plaintext storage by major platforms, and the systematic failure of “military-grade encryption” marketing to address architectural reality.

The analysis introduces the concept of “Rollup Rot”—the accumulation of elementary vulnerabilities such as Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR) and absent API rate limits within venture-backed M&A platforms—and traces its root cause to the principal-agent problem embedded in executive compensation structures. By contrasting the catastrophic operational meltdown of Southwest Airlines with the proactive decade-long core modernization of Zions Bancorp, the report demonstrates that technical debt is not an engineering failure but a governance failure. The paper concludes by arguing that the adoption of Zero-Knowledge architectures and the fundamental restructuring of executive incentive plans represent the only viable paths to protecting the humans who depend on the global digital ecosystem.

title: Workload Matters: A Quantitative Examination of Caseload Reform & Job Satisfaction in South African Child Protection

detail.title: Workload Matters: A Quantitative Examination of Caseload Reform & Job Satisfaction in South African Child Protection
detail.abstract: ​​Background:Child protection in South Africa has long been characterized by unmanageable caseloads, escalating administrative workload, and chronic resource constraints. There remains a lack of quantitative evidence measuring how workload and caseload contribute to job satisfaction.Participants and Setting: This pilot study examined workload to identify a reasonable amount of cases for a full-time social worker. This study investigates how caseloads affect job satisfaction and service delivery. Child protection social workers (N=66) were sampled from 6 provinces in South Africa.Methods: A brief demographic questionnaire and the Child Welfare Employee Feedback Scale - Revised survey was distributed to child protection social workers at non-profit agencies within six provinces of South Africa using Qualtrics (Griffiths, Royse, Murphy, Jones, Culver, Turner, & Smajlovic; 2023). Quantitative data was analyzed using SPSS and descriptive analyses were performed along with non-parametric statistical tests. Results: The average caseload size for all participants (N=66) was 96.42, which is above the broadly recommended national guideline of 60 cases per month. Significant negative correlations were found between caseload size and job satisfaction (p < .05), indicating lower job satisfaction with larger caseloads. Job satisfaction varied significantly by province (Kruskal-Wallis H=11.147, p=.025) with an effect size of .45 (η² >  0.14), indicating a large effect size.Conclusions: Findings reveal systemic challenges with excessive caseloads and administrative burdens that have a negative effect on job satisfaction. Reforms are urgently needed to ensure ethical, sustainable working conditions and effective service delivery. The results provide an initial evidence-based justification for supporting workload reform.

title: Research on a Digital Risk Scoring Model for Cross-Border Transactions Integrating Buyer Behavior and Logistics Data

detail.title: Research on a Digital Risk Scoring Model for Cross-Border Transactions Integrating Buyer Behavior and Logistics Data
detail.abstract: With the rapid growth of cross-border B2B transactions, the digital capabilities of platform risk control have become a critical component in ensuring transaction security.This study constructs a cross-border transaction risk scoring model integrating buyer behavioral characteristics with logistics temperature control data, using high-value wine exports as a representative application scenario. Modeling was performed using data from 26,000 buyers, 138,000 orders, and approximately 350,000 logistics records. The feature system encompasses order frequency, payment delay rate, price structure, dispute history, node dwell time, and temperature deviation frequency.Comparative modeling using LightGBM, XGBoost, and logistic regression revealed that incorporating logistics and environmental features increased the model's AUC by approximately 11%, significantly enhancing high-risk order identification. This study validates the effectiveness of joint modeling using behavioral data and supply chain visualization data for risk control in cross-border e-commerce.

detail.abstract: Independent publishers operating on Amazon's Kindle Direct Publishing platform routinely misread their advertising profitability. The platform's native metric-Advertising Cost of Sale (ACOS)-measures only the ratio of ad spend to ad-attributed sales, systematically omitting three critical financial realities: the cannibalisation of organic sales by paid traffic (Ghost Profit), the true all-in cost of revenue including zero-conversion spend (True ACOR), and the 60-day cash lag between advertising deployment and royalty receipt. This paper presents the Publisher CFO framework-a structured capital allocation and risk management protocol designed to surface all three omissions, enforce discipline across a leveraged IP portfolio, and prevent the three principal failure modes that destroy publisher profitability. The framework is validated through five years of primary longitudinal case study data across two publishing entities generating $76,459.28 in combined gross royalties from $25,875.67 in total advertising spend across nine international marketplaces. Publisher CFO is not an advertising optimisation tool. It is the risk management operating system for IP-Collateralised Rotating Credit Leverage-the capital architecture documented in the companion paper-in which intellectual property, consumer credit, and digital advertising infrastructure are combined to generate simultaneous operating yield, leverage amplification, currency carry, and inflation hedging returns. Without Publisher CFO, that architecture is dangerous. With it, it is institutional-grade capital allocation using consumer-grade instruments. This working paper documents a live operational case study and does not constitute financial advice.

title: E-Commerce Adoption on Small Businesses in Pokhara

detail.title: E-Commerce Adoption on Small Businesses in Pokhara
detail.abstract:
The growth of digital technology has changed the way businesses operate, especially for small enterprises seeking new opportunities for expansion. In Nepal, e-commerce is gradually emerging as an important business tool, yet its adoption among small businesses is still developing. This study explores the factors influencing e-commerce adoption among small businesses in Pokhara. Specifically, it examines how technological infrastructure, ease of use, customer demand, and competitive pressure shape the decision to adopt online platforms.

The research follows a descriptive design and is based primarily on data collected from 103 respondents through a structured questionnaire. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS, applying descriptive statistics and correlation analysis to understand the relationships between key variables.

The findings show that ease of use plays a crucial role in increasing customer demand, suggesting that simple and user-friendly platforms encourage greater online engagement. Competitive pressure also motivates businesses to improve their technological capabilities in order to remain relevant in the market. While most respondents are digitally familiar and actively engage in online shopping—primarily through smartphones—concerns regarding trust and delivery reliability continue to limit full confidence in e-commerce platforms.

Overall, the study highlights that improving usability, strengthening trust-building measures, enhancing delivery systems, and offering competitive pricing can significantly promote e-commerce adoption among small businesses. The results provide useful insights for entrepreneurs and policymakers aiming to support digital transformation and sustainable business growth in emerging economies.

title: Fusing Coercion and Capital at the Urban Scle: Singapore's Triadic Identity as a Sovereign Nationalistic City-State at the End of the Liberal World Order

detail.title: Fusing Coercion and Capital at the Urban Scle: Singapore's Triadic Identity as a Sovereign Nationalistic City-State at the End of the Liberal World Order
detail.abstract:
Singapore occupies a unique position in urban studies as the world's only city that is also a fully sovereign nation-state. Comparisons of various cities to Singapore are often vexed, I argue, because Singapore must be understood beyond mere urbanism and borrow from political science. 

This distinction is critical because Singapore's much-praised agency for collective action and state intervention is a downstream effect of what this global-nation-city-state developed for national/urban/state survival, broadly defined beyond militarisation and securitisation to economic success as a global city. 

This frame of understanding takes particular importance given the international situation in 2026. Geopolitics and military affairs rarely factor into urban studies because they are seen as separate spheres of study within international relations or security studies. As newspapers report on the death of the 'Dubai Myth' following the war against Iran, I can't help but think about how underemphasised diplomacy, securitisation, and state survival are in the academic understanding of Singapore as a successful metropolis. In the twilight of the liberal international order, where peace is no longer a guarantee, I seek to reassert the role of securitisation in the success and failure of cities, as their fates are tied to the nation-states that represent them.

detail.abstract: Using data from the 2010 birth cohort of the Longitudinal Survey of Newborns in the 21st Century, this paper examines how parental nonstandard work schedules (NSWS) and children's screen time are associated with children's weekday sleep duration, with particular attention to sex heterogeneity. The analysis reveals a modest but statistically significant reduction in daughters' weekday sleep (approximately 4 minutes per night), whereas no corresponding association is detected for sons. Paternal NSWS is not significantly related to sleep duration for either sex, a pattern that is consistent with limited variation and measurement constraints in fathers' work schedules in this dataset. Longer screen time (television viewing and video gaming) is strongly associated with shorter sleep for both boys and girls. Overall, the results suggest that the direct impact of parental NSWS on children's sleep is limited in magnitude, but that attention to children's screen use and family-friendly scheduling for mothers working nonstandard hours-especially in families with daughters-are likely to support healthier sleep habits.

title: Why Government Websites Must Enable AI-Mediated Access

detail.title: Why Government Websites Must Enable AI-Mediated Access
detail.abstract: AI-mediated search has become a primary channel through which citizens access government information, yet most federal agencies block AI crawlers by default. This paper argues that the failure to enable structured AI access carries measurable costs: degraded information quality for citizens, increased contact center demand, and lost return on existing digital investment. Drawing on organizational theory and federal law, the paper traces the failure to misaligned bureaucratic incentives and proposes four policy interventions: federal guidance from OMB and CISA establishing standards for AI crawler access; agency investment in AI-ready content; citation requirements as a condition of access; and enforcement through FITARA scorecard integration and the Authority to Operate process. The Government Publishing Office's Model Context Protocol server provides a federal precedent; what is missing is the policy framework to extend it government-wide.

detail.title: An Insight into Agroclimatic Determinants of Agricultural Productivity in Bihar
detail.abstract: Bihar is a predominantly agricultural state in India, which lagged in capturing the fruits of the green revolution due to improper water management and poor irrigational infrastructure. These variations have played a vital role in widening regional disparities across the districts. The lack of balanced regional development policies has also resulted in the carving out of minerals-rich districts in Jharkhand and left agriculture and allied activities as the lender to the last resort for the people of Bihar. The statewide implementation of three consecutive agricultural roadmaps during 2008-2022 has transformed the 'agricultural economy' to a certain extent. This paper analyses the pattern of change in the inter-district cropping pattern with the help of secondary data on area and production statistics by applying the 'crop concentration' and 'crop diversification' indices at five cross-sectional points of time i.e., 2001-02, 2006-07, 2011-12, 2016-17 and 2020-21. The spatial autocorrelation technique, 'Moran's I' was also applied to check any spatial clustering or dispersion in 'cropping patterns' and 'crop sector GDP' of the districts of Bihar. The results from the analysis show that particular districts specialized in the cultivation of specific crops or groups of crops and the positive-significant value of Moran's I also reflects the presence of spatial clustering across the regions. So, the region-specific policy implications have been outlined in the brief in this research.

title: Bitcoin as a Geopolitical Hedge: Evidence from the 2026 Venezuela and Iran Oil Shocks
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Bitcoin as a Geopolitical Hedge: Evidence from the 2026 Venezuela and Iran Oil Shocks
detail.abstract: This study evaluates whether Bitcoin functions as a hedge against inflationary shocks arising from geopolitical disruptions to global oil supply. Using daily data from January 20, 2025, through March 29, 2026, the analysis exploits two exogenous geopolitical events: the January 3, 2026, U.S. military operation in Venezuela and the February 28, 2026, coordinated U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran. These events generated oil price responses of markedly different magnitude and persistence, enabling identification of regime-dependent effects. The Venezuela event was quickly absorbed and interpreted as having limited supply-negative implications, while the Iran crisis produced a sustained oil price surge exceeding $110 per barrel. Employing regression analysis, asymmetric response modeling, and event study methodology controlling for equity market movements, the results indicate that Bitcoin behaves primarily as a high-beta risk asset during normal periods but exhibits conditional hedge-like characteristics during large, sustained geopolitical shocks. During the Iran crisis window, Bitcoin generated a cumulative abnormal return of 34.1% (p < 0.05), benchmarked against its historical relationship with the Nasdaq, even as gold fell 14.3% and the Nasdaq declined 7.4%. In contrast, the Venezuela episode provides little evidence of hedging behavior and instead reveals sensitivity to macroeconomic easing conditions, with Bitcoin rising sharply when oil prices fell (coefficient = 1.77, p < 0.001). These findings support a regime-dependent interpretation: Bitcoin's classification as either a speculative asset or a safe haven is incomplete without accounting for the scale and persistence of the underlying shock.

detail.abstract: This research investigates the challenges and implications of implementing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) in tobacco control policies in East Africa, focusing on six countries: Rwanda, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, and South Sudan. This research is crucial because of the potential conflict between AfCFTA’s trade liberalisation objectives and public health priorities concerning tobacco control. This study provides insights into the current landscape of tobacco control policies, the potential impact of AfCFTA on tobacco trade and consumption, and the challenges and opportunities for harmonising regulations and strengthening enforcement mechanisms. This study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining in-depth interviews, surveys, and desk reviews to gather data from various stakeholders, including policymakers, industry representatives, and civil society organisations. The desk review and stakeholder mapping revealed that, while East African countries have made strides in tobacco control, challenges persist, including illicit trade, industry interference, weak enforcement, and a lack of public awareness. These challenges could be exacerbated by AfCFTA’s trade liberalisation if not accompanied by robust and harmonised tobacco control measures. This study highlights several key aspects of tobacco control efforts, noting both progress and persistent challenges. Despite advancements have been made, issues such as illicit trade and industry interference continue to undermine public health goals. Discrepancies in tobacco control policies and enforcement capacities across the EAC expose gaps that hinder regional harmonisation efforts and create vulnerabilities that the tobacco industry can exploit. Economic and cultural factors also complicate enforcement as conflicting interests and norms often work against strict regulations. Additionally, limited resources and capacity pose substantial barriers to effectively implementing and enforcing tobacco control measures. The tobacco industry, alongside the prevalence of illicit trade, remains a significant threat, undermining policy efforts and impeding public health objectives across the region. The study recommends strengthening the enforcement of existing laws, increasing tobacco taxes and tariffs, implementing plain packaging and comprehensive bans on advertising, investing in cessation programs, and enhancing regional collaboration. To further understand the context of this study, the following section provides background information on the AfCFTA and its potential implications for tobacco control in East Africa

detail.abstract: This working paper argues that data-driven supervision (DDS) provides a principled and practical resolution to the tension between supervisory convergence and institutional decentralisation at the heart of the current EU debate on supervisory architecture. Rather than forcing a binary choice between centralised EU-level supervision and the status quo, DDS enables a collegial centralisation of risk identification, metric definition, and supervisory expectations while preserving operational decentralisation of day-today supervision. The paper formalises supervision as a problem of statistical inference under measurement error and resource constraints, and proposes a five-step supervisory cycle through which a decentralised network of National Competent Authorities can achieve common risk identification, shared metrics, harmonised data standards, consistent triage, and continuous collegial calibration. The SPMU (Severity, Persistence, Materiality, Uncertainty) composite scoring architecture provides the analytical core. The paper analyses the economics of DDS-demonstrating scale economies, multi-mission amortisation, and early-intervention savings-and develops the governance, model-risk, and institutional-sustainability requirements for sustainable deployment. The central conclusion is that, for market segments characterised by large dispersed populations under harmonised EU legislation, a decentralised DDS architecture delivers effective, convergent, and proportionate supervision at lower institutional cost and with fewer transition risks than full centralisation of supervisory powers.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the effect of the 2025 U.S. import tariffs on import prices and local labor-markets. To that end, we use highly disaggregated customs data to construct realized tariff rates from actual duty collections, rather than announced statutory schedules. An important contribution is that we document a large and persistent gap between the two measures, driven by within-country product reallocation, cross-country sourcing shifts, and implementation frictions. This implies that statutory rates are a poor proxy for the trade shock that firms actually faced. Using realized tariffs, we find that pass-through of realized tariffs into import prices was close to one hundred percent, with negligible adjustment by foreign exporters and a significant reduction in import quantities. When we examine local labor-market consequences of the increase in import tariffs, we find that counties which are more exposed to import-competing sectors experienced small declines in unemployment and that rising input costs weighed marginally on labor-force participation. Both effects, though heterogeneous across space, are economically negligible. In contrast to the 2018–2019 tariff episode, where rising input costs dominated, resulting in lower manufacturing employment, the 2025 tariffs did not generate large labor-market changes in either direction.

detail.abstract:
The report reviews the global transition finance landscape, examining the importance of multistakeholder collaborations and international best practices in preventing greenwashing and maintaining transparency. Based on a survey and in-depth interviews commissioned by the HKIMR, the study captures insights from a diverse range of global stakeholders—including financial institutions and multilateral organisations—offering a detailed analysis of the current state, emerging trends, and future trajectory of the international transition finance ecosystem.

The study reveals a clear momentum in transition finance, with 60% of survey respondents already either active in or exploring transition finance developments. Among a diverse range of financial instruments, equity and fund investments as well as debt instruments were the most commonly used tools to channel capital towards transition projects. As the ecosystem progressively matures, a gradual shift towards more specialised instruments is anticipated. Respondents further observed that collaborative models, including blended finance approaches, can draw in private capital by enhancing the risk-return profiles of investments in transition projects.

The study also indicates that market outlook is cautiously optimistic, with 74% of respondents anticipating a stable or growing global transition finance market over the next three years. Positive sentiment is most pronounced in the Asia-Pacific region, where 91% of respondents expected stability or growth. Finally, the study outlines several considerations, including maintaining a high level of regulatory and policy clarity, and deepening regional collaborations, to support the development of a vibrant transition finance ecosystem in Hong Kong.

detail.abstract: We study the causal effect of the local supply of sector-specific innovators on patenting activity across US metropolitan areas, distinguishing between innovators active in carbon-intensive ("brown") and environmentally sustainable ("green") technological fields. Using USPTO patent data from 1990 to 2016, we document a marked shift in the geography of green innovation: while brown patenting has long been concentrated in established hubs, green patents-initially more dispersed-have increasingly converged toward the same locations. We build a theoretical framework in which local patenting activity is driven by the supply of green and brown innovators, investigating how their interaction shapes the innovation process. Empirically, we address endogeneity using a shift-share instrument that combines predetermined local technological specialization with exogenous shocks to foreign innovation across CPC sections. We find that a one-unit increase in the local supply of brown innovators raises patenting activity by approximately 0.8%, an effect that is robust across specifications. Together, these findings suggest that green innovation is becoming increasingly embedded in existing agglomeration ecosystems, with important implications for place-based climate policy.

detail.abstract: We introduce Exploratory Modelling and Analysis (EMA) as a framework for macroeconomic scenario analysis under deep uncertainty. EMA traces scenarios of interest from policy‑relevant outcomes. These outcomes are forecasted by a model, based on a large set of uncertain conditioning variables. This approach flips the conventional method of scenario analysis, by sampling many scenarios without imposing strong ex‑ante priors on the choice, combination, value, or distribution of the conditioning variables. Applying EMA with an interacted VAR model to financial stress scenarios for the euro area shows that scenarios of interest can be uncovered that may be overlooked by common approaches for scenario analysis.

title: Walk Forward Correlation A Diagnostic for Over-Fitting and Structural Edge in Trading Strategy Optimisation

detail.title: Walk Forward Correlation A Diagnostic for Over-Fitting and Structural Edge in Trading Strategy Optimisation
detail.abstract: This paper introduces Walk Forward Correlation (WFC), a diagnostic technique for assessing both over-fitting and the presence of genuine structural edge in trading strategy optimisation. Traditional single-stage walk-forward validation and multi-stage Walk Forward Analysis [1] (WFA) evaluate only the single parameter set selected as most robust or optimal during each in-sample (IS) optimisation window. This approach can lead to false confidence when the chosen parameters perform well out-of-sample (OOS) purely by chance. Over-fitting and selection bias in financial modelling have been extensively documented [2-4]. WFC evaluates the entire optimisation surface by computing performance metrics for all parameter combinations across both IS and OOS datasets, and then measuring the correlation between IS and OOS performance across the full n-dimensional parameter space. A high positive correlation indicates that IS performance is predictive of OOS performance, suggesting that over-fitting has been effectively constrained. A low or near-zero correlation indicates that IS performance contains little or no information about OOS behaviour, implying over-fitting or the absence of structural edge. The behaviour of WFC is demonstrated using multiple realworld optimisation datasets, and its implications for robustness assessment, structural edge identification, and parameter-space topology are discussed.

detail.title: Mitigating Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models via Cross-Layer Visual Anchors
detail.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models often suffer from hallucination. While existing research utilizes attention enhancement and visual retracing, we find these works lack sufficient interpretability regarding attention drift in final model stages. In this paper, we investigate the layer wise evolution of visual features and discover that hallucination stems from deep layer attention regressing toward initial visual noise from early layers. We observe that output reliability depends on acquiring visual anchors at intermediate layers rather than final layers. Based on these insights, we propose CLVA, which stands for Cross-Layer Visual Anchors, a training free method that reinforces critical mid layer features while suppressing regressive noise. This approach effectively pulls deep layer attention back to correct visual regions by utilizing essential anchors captured from attention dynamics. We evaluate our method across diverse architectures and benchmarks, demonstrating outstanding performance without significant increase in computational time and GPU memory.

title: Industrial Patent Law

detail.title: Industrial Patent Law
detail.abstract:
History is absent from the rigorous debate on government patent policy. Scholarship has focused on the Bayh-Dole Act of 1980, where the government relinquished control over patents on inventions developed with federal funding. The act’s critics advocate the exercise of its key exception: government rights to “march in” to require that contractors license patents to third parties, a carveout never used until last year, when the Trump Administration threatened to exercise it against universities. Meanwhile, the act’s defenders argue that marching in and other “public patent powers”—e.g., government rights to title or liability shields for contractors—stymy innovation and commercialization and are not designed to serve the public interest. But these debates have hardly examined the world before Bayh-Dole, when government control of patents was the norm. Scholars instead study the act’s effects, such as “anticommons” problems, or engage in counterfactuals, asking what might have transpired if the government had ever marched in or exercised similar powers. Yet history supplies an economic experiment for testing the effects of powers like march-in before Bayh-Dole. The most influential and striking uses of these powers involved one of the consequential technologies of the Cold War, the communications satellite.

To that end, this Essay is a targeted account of industrial patent law, the post-World War II framework for government patent policy. Carefully reading archival records, administrative proceedings, and case law on patents and contracts during the Cold War, the Essay uncovers the history of industrial patent law and bolsters the argument for its restoration. The Essay focuses on disputes over communications satellites, which shaped industrial patent law writ large.

The Essay draws three takeaways from this history. First, industrial patent law was designed and worked to spur innovation and commercialization and protect the public interest, contrary to the narrative spun by skeptics of march-in rights. Second, industrial patent law’s demise was due not merely to Bayh-Dole, but, more profoundly, to the government’s longstanding belief in unsubstantiated claims from company representatives that public patent powers are anathema to technological and commercial growth—claims recited by skeptics of march-in rights to this day. Third, the history supports two modern uses of industrial patent law: (1) marching in as an antimonopoly tool to control price; and (2) retaining title or marching in to regulate spacecraft as public utilities, an application highly pertinent to SpaceX. The Essay also suggests that, contrary to scholarly outcry, the Trump Administration’s threat to march in on universities is an opportunity to course correct decades of unchecked privatization of U.S. research.

detail.abstract: Using 41.6 million trades, we measure adverse selection in prediction markets. Adapting Kyle's λ and the Glosten-Harris decomposition, we show single-name markets exhibit greater informed price impact than broad-based markets. Despite this, effective spreads are only modestly wider, and market makers earn twice as much per contract. A frequency-magnitude decomposition resolves this puzzle: traders systematically overbet YES in markets that predominantly settle NO, generating a behavioral surplus that cross-subsidizes adverse selection. Adapting the VPIN toxicity metric, we find that one-sided order flow predicts maker losses in single-name markets but not broad-based markets. Our research suggests a new microstructure equilibrium concept for bilateral settlement markets.

title: Why Feldstein-Horioka Correlations Vary: Demographics and the Savings Retention Puzzle

detail.title: Why Feldstein-Horioka Correlations Vary: Demographics and the Savings Retention Puzzle
detail.abstract: The Feldstein-Horioka puzzle-the surprisingly high correlation between national savings and investment-has defied explanation for 45 years. We show that the pooled savings retention coefficient masks enormous demographic heterogeneity. Using an expanded panel of up to 170 countries over 1990-2024, we find that the baseline pooled retention coefficient of 0.054 averages across two very different regimes: aging economies with strong savings-investment links (home bias, pension fund allocation, mature financial systems) and young economies where domestic savings and investment are only weakly related (foreign capital finances investment, savings are too small to drive accumulation). When we interact the savings rate with the Z1 demographic polynomial-an aging index where higher values correspond to older populations (e.g., Japan = +1.67, Nigeria =-3.20)-the retention coefficient at the demographic mean rises to 0.259 and the S x Z1 interaction is +2.32 (p < 0.001), with R-squared rising from 0.071 to 0.180. The positive interaction means aging economies retain more of each marginal dollar saved for domestic investment. The result strengthens at longer horizons (3.30 at 5 years, 3.50 at 10 years), survives income-level controls, and holds within both low-and high-income subsamples. Demographics and financial openness (KAOPEN) independently weaken the pooled coefficient, but their multiplicative interaction is insignificant (p = 0.390). These findings suggest that the original high FH coefficient reflected the demographic composition of early OECD samples-mature economies with strong home bias-and the secular decline reflects the expansion of the global sample to include younger economies with weaker savings-investment links. This interpretation is consistent with our cross-sectional results, though we do not separately decompose the time trend into composition versus integration effects.

title: Parallel Cross-Verification of Large Language Models for Rapid Theoretical Development: Evidence from an Overnight Economics

detail.title: Parallel Cross-Verification of Large Language Models for Rapid Theoretical Development: Evidence from an Overnight Economics
detail.abstract: This paper documents a reproducible workflow in which a single human researcher uses three frontier large language models (LLMs) in parallel-via manual copy-paste between isolated sessions-to accelerate theoretical work in economics. The case study is the companion paper "Public vs. Private Information under Fixed Total Precision", completed from initial idea to SSRN-ready manuscript in a single overnight session of approximately 6.5 hours of active human time. By deliberately surfacing and resolving disagreements among the models, the method turned inconsistency into a powerful error-detection mechanism. Four substantive errors that likely would have survived a first solo draft were identified and corrected. The paper provides an honest timeline, exact prompts, observed failure modes, and a taxonomy of research tasks by AI suitability. The workflow is immediately replicable in any sufficiently formal domain and requires no direct model-to-model communication.

title: BOJ Exit as Natural Experiment for the Safe Asset Cliff: Does the JGB Market Reprice Demographic Fiscal Risk?

detail.title: BOJ Exit as Natural Experiment for the Safe Asset Cliff: Does the JGB Market Reprice Demographic Fiscal Risk?
detail.abstract: The Bank of Japan's sequential exit from yield curve control (YCC) and negative interest rate policy (NIRP) between December 2022 and January 2025 provides a natural experiment for testing whether sovereign bond markets reprice the demographic fiscal risk identified in Peters (2024, Paper 17). Using a market-model event study on daily JGB 10-year yields across six BOJ policy events, I find statistically significant abnormal yield increases concentrated in the surprise events: +23.3bp (t = 14.73, p < 0.01) for the December 2022 YCC band widening and +15.0bp (t = 3.72, p < 0.01) for the July 2023 band expansion. Cumulative abnormal returns across all six events total +46.5bp in the [-1,+1] window (t = 4.77, p < 0.01). All six events produce Japan-specific spread widening against US Treasuries, with cumulative JGB-UST spread expansion of +88bp, confirming the repricing is not a global rate phenomenon. Connecting the event study to the OADR spline framework from Paper 17, I estimate Japan's demographic yield gap at 119bp. The total JGB yield increase of 218bp from pre-exit levels overshoots this gap (183% closure), while the event-window CARs alone account for 39% of the gap. These findings suggest that the BOJ's unconventional policies were suppressing a demographically driven yield premium, and that its removal is consistent with the safe asset cliff thesis: aging economies face rising borrowing costs once monetary accommodation is withdrawn. N = 9,835 daily observations; 6 events; 140-country cross-section for yield-rating benchmarking.

detail.title: Blinded by Smog? How Air Pollution Drives Predictable Return Patterns
detail.abstract: This study investigates how local air pollution affects stock prices and market efficiency. Deterioration in air quality during weekends predicts a significant negative return for local brown stocks on the first subsequent trading day, followed by a positive reversal. Using proprietary account-level brokerage records, we trace the underlying mechanism and show that air pollution shocks capture the attention of local retail investors, who exert immediate selling pressure on brown stocks. This temporary mispricing is then arbitraged by sophisticated investors, whose net buying drives the reversal. Our findings link environmental shocks to specific investor trading patterns that generate predictable return dynamics.

title: The Impact of Individual Alcohol Prohibition on Crime and Poor Relief in Early Twentieth-Century Sweden
affiliations: Umeå University, Umeå University and Jonkoping University

detail.title: The Impact of Individual Alcohol Prohibition on Crime and Poor Relief in Early Twentieth-Century Sweden
detail.abstract: In the early twentieth century, reformers across Europe and North America viewed alcohol misuse as a major source of poverty, crime, and welfare dependency, prompting many countries to adopt prohibition policies. Sweden followed a distinct path by introducing a system of individual prohibition, formalized nationally in 1917 but implemented earlier in several cities between 1912 and 1915. Rather than banning alcohol universally, the policy selectively restricted access to strong liquor for individuals deemed at risk of welfare dependency or criminality. Despite the central role of these claims in shaping policy, little empirical evidence exists on whether individual prohibition achieved its intended objectives to reduce crime and poverty. This study evaluates the regulation by examining outcomes policymakers explicitly sought to influence. To address causal identification, we exploit variation in the timing of individual prohibition, as several cities adopted the policy prior to national reform. Using 1910s city-level panel data, we estimate the short-term effects on alcohol sales, crime, and poor relief. The results show that strong liquor sales declined by about 20 percent during the first two years, accompanied by a 21 percent reduction in arrests for drunkenness relative to control cities. Theft and breaches of peace also decreased, while violent crime remained unaffected. Despite these reductions in consumption and certain alcohol-related offences, individual prohibition did not affect poverty in the short-run: neither the stock nor the inflow of poor-relief recipients changed.

title: The Externalities of Private Tutoring on Students' Academic and Noncognitive Outcomes: Evidence and Mechanisms

detail.title: The Externalities of Private Tutoring on Students' Academic and Noncognitive Outcomes: Evidence and Mechanisms
detail.abstract: This paper examines the spillover effects of private tutoring on students' academic and noncognitive outcomes in the classroom. Utilizing nationally representative data of middle school students randomly assigned to classes in China, we find that students receiving private tutoring have negative impacts on peers' academic performance and noncognitive skills. We provide evidence that these effects operate through damaging the classroom environment and reducing student effort, instead of affecting teachers' effort or teaching styles. Furthermore, we find that these effects are more pronounced among male students, students with a rural hukou, students from lower socioeconomic backgrounds, and students with lower ability. Our findings suggest that the rat race in private tutoring during compulsory education may exacerbate educational inequality.

title: Consolidation Driven De-Branching: Overlap Effects in Quasi-Exogenous Bank M&A

detail.title: Consolidation Driven De-Branching: Overlap Effects in Quasi-Exogenous Bank M&A
detail.abstract: I isolate the consolidation channel of bank de-branching using FDIC Purchase-and-Assumption resolutions, in which failed banks are transferred to solvent acquirers through regulator-driven auctions completed within days. A stacked Difference-in-Differences design compares branch adjustments across overlap, expansion, and acquirer-only counties within the same resolution event. Branch growth in overlap counties falls by 12.4 percentage points in the first post-resolution year and remains depressed through year three, with a cumulative decline of approximately 26%. No comparable immediate contraction occurs elsewhere. The effect does not scale with overlap intensity, indicating that geographic duplication, rather than its degree, drives the result. Because expansion counties absorb target-side distress, the estimated decline isolates consolidation from financial fragility and technological substitution.

title: Charting the Landscape of Person-Centered Care in Ghana: A Scoping Review of Evidence and Current Practices

detail.title: Charting the Landscape of Person-Centered Care in Ghana: A Scoping Review of Evidence and Current Practices

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.

detail.abstract:
Background: Person-centered care (PCC)—defined as care that is respectful of and responsive to individuals’ preferences, needs, and values—is a cornerstone of high-quality healthcare. While there is a global momentum toward PCC, evidence from Ghana—especially beyond maternal health—remains limited. This scoping review aims to: (1) examine the extent of PCC research in Ghana; (2) evaluate documented PCC; (3) identify patient expectations and preferences; (4) explore barriers and enablers to PCC; (5) assess intervention effectiveness; and (6) highlight research gaps.

Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception to July 2024. Eligible studies included quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method research assessing PCC across all healthcare levels, specialties, and conditions in Ghana.  All titles, abstracts, and full texts were assessed by at least two reviewers. Dimensions of PCC—such as dignity and respect, communication and autonomy, supportive care, patient satisfaction, and experiences of mistreatment or discrimination—were extracted using a standardized template.

Results: Our initial search yielded 3076 articles, of which 143 publications were included. Most studies revealed significant gaps in core aspects of PCC, as the majority of reports reflected negative patient experiences—especially in communication (84.6% negative), dignity and respect (75.4%), and privacy (78.3%). Stakeholder perceptions echoed similar concerns, with unmet patient expectations in communication, involvement in care, and timely service. Barriers to PCC included inadequate patient education and empowerment, poor provider attitudes and communication, and poor care coordination. Facilitators included staff training, increased staffing, improved infrastructure, and supportive provider attitudes. Eight intervention studies were identified, with some showing improvements in PCC.

Conclusions: The scoping review highlights widespread negative perceptions of PCC in Ghana and consistently unmet patient expectations. Barriers and facilitators span patient, provider, healthcare system, and sociocultural levels, with few robust PCC interventions identified. The findings, therefore, emphasize the urgent need to translate PCC principles into practice within Ghana’s healthcare system.

title: Human Digital Twins and Proxy-Based Production: The Legal Object Law Has Not Named
affiliations: and

detail.title: Human Digital Twins and Proxy-Based Production: The Legal Object Law Has Not Named

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors received no external funding for the research or writing of this Article and report no conflicts of interest.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in the Columbia Human Rights Law Review (2026-2027)

detail.abstract:
AI is shifting from prediction and automation to substitution. Systems trained on an individual’s records can now generate outputs in that individual’s voice and style and circulate them as operational guidance. In the workplace, this substitution increasingly takes the form of human digital twins, worker-specific models that others can consult and rely on as stand-ins for the worker’s own input. That shift destabilizes core premises of labor and employment law: that work and workplace decisions remain attributable to the worker who performs them, and that work is bounded in time with a meaningful capacity to withdraw.

This Article offers the first sustained labor-and-employment account of human digital twins as a governance architecture at work. It defines workplace human digital twins as computational models of specific workers that are trained on work-linked data and updated over time and are deployed to generate outputs that others can treat as substitutes for the worker’s own input. It argues that this architecture unsettles foundational features of labor and employment law and identifies the pressure points it creates. Human digital twins destabilize working time by enabling value to be produced through a worker-anchored operational proxy beyond presence and clock time. They reconfigure privacy, autonomy, and identity by requiring pervasive capture of workplace communications and decision patterns. They unsettle attribution by blurring the line between worker agency and algorithmic output, complicating responsibility for harm and control over proxy-generated value. Because key choices are being made now, before defaults harden, the Article advances a regulatory framework calibrated to identity-intensive proxy use. That framework would treat workplace human digital twins as an ecosystem rather than an employer-owned tool, allocate rights and responsibilities across employers and vendors based on control and benefit, and regulate along a continuum keyed to identity intensity. When a system crosses the proxy threshold by operating as a representational stand-in that others rely on in ordinary workflows, the framework requires tighter limits, including nonwaivable boundary rules and a meaningful, revocable employee veto supported by vendor-facing obligations tied to system design and updates. The aim is to set enforceable limits before proxy-based production becomes a settled workplace default.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination for Cervical Cancer Prevention in Palestine: A Model-Based Analysis

detail.abstract:
Background: Cervical cancer is a largely preventable malignancy driven by persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. In Palestine, molecular studies demonstrate a high burden of HPV, with HPV16/18 accounting for 42.5% of cancers, yet no national vaccination program exists. This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of HPV vaccination to inform national policy.

Methods; A Markov state-transition model compared routine vaccination of girls aged 9-14 years (9-valent vaccine) against no vaccination. The analysis adopted a health-system perspective, lifetime horizon, 3% annual discounting, and half-cycle correction. Transition probabilities were calibrated to local epidemiological data. Costs reflected local Ministry of Health tariffs. Both deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses (PSA) were conducted.

Results: For a cohort of 65,000 girls, the two-dose program yielded an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of USD 9,121 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained. A one-dose scenario improved the ICER to USD 4,610 per QALY gained. Interpreted against a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of 3x GDP per capita (USD ~$11,400), the two-dose strategy is cost-effective, while the one-dose strategy approaches the 1x GDP per capita threshold for high cost-effectiveness. PSA demonstrated a >85% probability of the intervention being cost-effective at the 3x GDP threshold.

Conclusions: Introducing HPV vaccination in Palestine is economically efficient. Policy makers should prioritize negotiated vaccine pricing and consider one-dose schedules to maximize affordability and health impact within constrained budgets.

title: Tokenized Deposits, Zero-Knowledge Disclosure, and Bank Runs: How Blockchain Infrastructure Reshapes Financial Fragility
affiliations: University of South Carolina

detail.title: Tokenized Deposits, Zero-Knowledge Disclosure, and Bank Runs: How Blockchain Infrastructure Reshapes Financial Fragility
detail.abstract: Tokenized deposits settle continuously and nearly instantaneously, but faster withdrawal execution compresses the coordination game among depositors and increases funding fragility even for solvent banks. This paper examines how disclosure design interacts with settlement speed to determine run risk and welfare in tokenized banking environments. We compare conventional disclosure with verifiable compliance disclosure implemented via Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), which allow banks to certify regulatory liquidity compliance without revealing precise balance sheet positions. ZKP disclosure eliminates coordination-driven runs on compliant banks by pooling institutions near the regulatory threshold, at the cost of weaker market discipline as sophisticated depositors acquire less private information. A calibrated simulation using FDIC call report data for large US commercial banks, including the five Cari Network members, quantifies run probabilities and welfare across settlement speeds and depositor compositions. Tokenization without enhanced disclosure amplifies fragility; combining fast settlement with verifiable compliance disclosure improves welfare, particularly for retail-oriented funding bases. Disclosure architecture is not ancillary to tokenized deposit regulation, it is central to it.

title: 노인돌봄 인력의 전망과 정책 대응 (Who Cares for Us?: Policies on Eldercare Workers)

detail.title: 노인돌봄 인력의 전망과 정책 대응 (Who Cares for Us?: Policies on Eldercare Workers)

publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Development Institute (KDI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Korean Abstract: 
노인돌봄 일자리는 노동집약적이며 감정 소모적인 동시에 저숙련자가 비교적 쉽게 진입할 수 있는 저임금 일자리이다. 이런 이유로 전 세계적으로 노인돌봄 일자리는 선호도가 낮으며, 고령화가 진행된 선진국들은 서비스 인력 부족 문제를 겪고 있다. 우리나라는 2024년 12월 65세 이상 고령인구가 전체 인구의 20% 이상을 차지하는 초고령사회로 진입하였다. 또한 베이비붐 세대가 75세 이상 후기 고령자로 진입하는 2030년 이후에는 노인돌봄서비스가 필요한 초고령인구 규모가 빠른 증가세를 나타내면서 노인돌봄 분야의 수급 불균형 문제가 가까운 시일 내에 심화될 것으로 예상된다.

본 연구는 우리나라 노인돌봄서비스 인력의 현황과 한계를 확인하고 노인돌봄 인력 정책의 개선 방향을 제안하는 것을 목표로 한다. 이를 위해 노인돌봄 인력 수급 추계를 통해 앞으로 부족한 인력의 규모를 전망하고 인력 확충 정책 대응 방향에 대해 논의한다. 또한 인력의 양적, 질적 확충이 노인의 삶의 질 개선에 미친 영향을 실증분석하고, 이를 통해 현재 노인돌봄 인력 정책의 개선 방향을 제안하는 것을 목표로 한다.

English Abstract: 
South Korea reached the super-aged mark in December 2024, with over 20% of its population aged 65 and older. Eldercare jobs, labor-intensive and emotionally demanding yet accessible to low-skilled workers at low wages, are globally undesirable, leading to labor shortages in advanced economies. As baby boomers (born 1955-1963) enter the late elderly (75 and older) after 2030, demand for eldercare services is projected to surge, worsening supply-demand imbalances.

This study examines the current state and limitations of Korea’s eldercare workforce to propose policy improvements. It estimates eldercare labor supply and demand to forecast the scale of labor shortage and discusses strategies for workforce expansion. Additionally, an empirical analysis assesses how quantitative and qualitative workforce expansion impacts the quality of life for residents in long-term care facilities, providing policy insights.

title: Sanrim-gye: A Local Community that Contributed to Reforestation through Public-Private Partnership
affiliations: Seoul National University

detail.title: Sanrim-gye: A Local Community that Contributed to Reforestation through Public-Private Partnership

publicationDetails.detailsText: KDI School of Pub Policy & Management Paper No. WP26-08
publicationDetails.journalName: KDI School of Public Policy & Management Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Among Korea’s old village traditions was dure—a cooperative labor system designed to facilitate mutual assistance and mitigate the hardships of agricultural life. In addition, to manage limited forest resources efficiently, villagers established song-gye (松契), communal associations dedicated to the organized procurement of fuel and timber. Following the nation’s liberation, in an effort to restore the devastated forests, the government encouraged—on a legal basis— the formation of sanrim-gye (山林契), village-based forestry cooperatives. The sanrim-gye independently established rules to maintain local order, including mountain patrols, the prevention of illegal logging, and the conservation of forest ecosystems. These associations also oversaw the systematic production of green manure and the collection of fuel. The establishment of fuelwood forests and the reforestation of village hillsides were carried out directly by the sanrim-gye; meanwhile, the government provided essential inputs—such as seedlings and fertilizer—free of charge and utilized the Saemaul Undong to educate the public on the imperative of forest restoration. To incentivize reforestation and strengthen the sanrim-gye, the government introduced several institutional measures: for private forests, profit-sharing and entrusted forest schemes; for public forests, forest-leasing schemes; and for national forests, a free-transfer scheme. These measures provided strong economic incentives for sanrim-gye, generating significant momentum for active tree planting and forest management across different forms of ownership. Large-scale, government-led erosion-control projects also mobilized labor through the sanrim-gye, and, by paying wages, created employment for poor members. Such forms of public–private cooperative governance laid the groundwork for the government’s First and Second 10-Year Forest Rehabilitation Plans (1973–1987) to proceed smoothly and ultimately achieve nationwide reforestation. The effectiveness of these arrangements demonstrates that the sanrim-gye system closely aligns with Elinor Ostrom’s principles for successful common-pool resource (CPR) management, illustrating the capacity of local communities to govern shared resources effectively. The inscription of Korea’s reforestation records on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register in April 2025 provides international validation of Korea’s reforestation efforts as a model case within the global environmental movement, underscoring both the historical nsignificance and organizational strength of the sanrim-gye. Given its high degree of universality, objectivity, and transparency, Korea’s sanrim-gye offers a robust framework that can be adapted to developing countries with different traditions and cultures.

title: Recursive Portfolio Machines
affiliations: , Yale SOM, Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Recursive Portfolio Machines

publicationDetails.detailsText: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper No. 26-36
publicationDetails.journalName: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We introduce the Recursive Portfolio Machine (RPM), an asset-pricing framework for learning the characteristic directions most relevant for the stochastic discount factor (SDF). Our theory shows that the risk-weighted gradient outer product (RWGOP) recovers the pricing-relevant subspace of characteristic space, while its eigenvectors define principal pricing directions that rank this subspace by pricing importance. The RPM operationalizes this theory by first estimating the RWGOP and then using it within a closed-form large factor model to construct the SDF. In U.S. equity data, the RPM improves out-of-sample performance relative to benchmark models. Low-rank versions retain much of the full-rank performance, suggesting that the pricing-relevant space is effectively low-dimensional.

title: Data-Driven Supervision and the Reduction of Supervisory Burden. A Conceptual and Operational Framework for National Competent Authorities
affiliations: Commission de Surveillance Du Secteur Financier

detail.title: Data-Driven Supervision and the Reduction of Supervisory Burden. A Conceptual and Operational Framework for National Competent Authorities

publicationDetails.journalName: BAFFI Centre on Economics, Finance & Regulation Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Financial supervisors are doing more with less. Over the past fifteen years, mandates have multiplied-covering prudential soundness, conduct, market integrity, operational resilience, and systemic risk-while supervised populations have grown and budgets have not kept pace. The resulting capacity gap is structural, not cyclical. This paper proposes data-driven supervision (DDS) as a scalable response. DDS converts regulatory reporting data into reproducible risk indicators, composite scores, and automated triage pathways, concentrating expert judgment where it adds most value. Because marginal costs per entity are low and infrastructure is reusable across supervisory missions, DDS generates economies of scale that traditional inspection-based approaches cannot. The paper develops formal frameworks for indicator design and triage, documents how regulatory reporting enables population-scale risk detection, and shows how a shared data infrastructure can serve multiple supervisory objectives simultaneously. Governance challenges-model risk, false positives, preservation of human judgment-are addressed directly, and a phased implementation roadmap for National Competent Authorities is presented. The analysis is candid about limits: DDS depends on data quality, complements rather than replaces traditional supervision, and requires active management of implementation risk.

title: Energy-Efficient Biomass Cookstoves and the Rebound: Evidence from Field Experiments in Rwanda and Senegal
affiliations: RWI Leibniz Institute for Economic Research, RWI  Leibniz Institute for Economic Research  and RWI - Leibniz Institute for Economic Research

detail.title: Energy-Efficient Biomass Cookstoves and the Rebound: Evidence from Field Experiments in Rwanda and Senegal

publicationDetails.journalName: United States Association for Energy Economics (USAEE) & International Association for Energy Economics (IAEE) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: In developing countries, energy-efficient biomass cookstoves lower the marginal cost of food preparation, thereby inducing households to cook more and offsetting part of the expected energy savings. This paper examines such rebound effects and their implications for energy and food consumption, drawing on the randomized distribution of energy-efficient biomass cookstoves to households free of charge in rural Rwanda and Senegal. Our estimations benefit from the exogenous variation in cooking efficiency due to the randomized assignment of the stoves. For both samples, we find a statistically significant and substantial reduction in energy use among treated households. In the Senegalese sample, this reduction is offset by a moderate rebound effect ranging between 16% and 25%. For the Rwandan sample, we find no statistically significant rebound effect. We discuss mechanisms that potentially drive these differences and the implications for rebound research and energy access policy.

Using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag(ARDL) for the regression analysis, it was discovered that foreign direct investment had a positive implication on the GDP in the short run and a negative effect in the long run while poverty rate had a favorable influence in both the short run and the long run. title: Demand-Driven Technical Change: Evidence from WFH Technologies
affiliations: Stanford University,  and Stanford University

detail.title: Demand-Driven Technical Change: Evidence from WFH Technologies
detail.abstract:
COVID-19 brought a sharp, unanticipated increase in the usefulness and value of technologies that support work from home (WFH). To investigate how this shock influenced the direction of technical change, we examine the text in 5.6 million U.S. patent applications published from 2010 to 2026. The share of patent applications that advances technologies in support of WFH rose by about two thirds within three years after the pandemic struck and remains about 50% above pre-pandemic levels five years later. The lasting rise in the WFH share of new applications concentrates in telecommunications – especially video conferencing, speech recognition, and audio processing. It is driven overwhelmingly by US corporations rather than foreign assignees or universities. In short, we find evidence that a sudden, lasting rise in WFH redirected innovation to technologies that support it.

title: Terminal Value under Piecewise-Linear Growth Rate
affiliations: McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management and Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC Barcelona Tech)

detail.title: Terminal Value under Piecewise-Linear Growth Rate
detail.abstract: This paper presents a terminal-value model in which cash-flow growth evolves through three intervals: an initial period of constant growth, a transition period in which the proportional growth rate declines linearly, and a terminal period of constant stable growth. We derive a closed-form expression for the present value of the cash-flow stream over the transition interval and an explicit formula for the cash-flow rate at the start of the terminal perpetuity. The framework can be generalized to richer piecewise specifications of cashflow growth. The model is formulated in continuous time: the discount rate and the growth rates are expressed as continuously compounded rates, and cash flow at each instant is represented as an instantaneous annual flow rate. We also provide the corresponding conversions from effective rates and show how the continuous-time cash-flow rate can be reconciled with the discrete cash flows used in the explicit forecast period.

title: If You Build It, They May Not Come: Willingness to Participate in Managed EV Charging

detail.title: If You Build It, They May Not Come: Willingness to Participate in Managed EV Charging
detail.abstract:
Despite the importance of program participation for policy, treatment effects are often measured on self-selected samples. We study electric vehicle (EV) managed charging, intended to reduce electric grid strain by optimally allocating charging across EVs. Prior work finds large impacts of managed charging among households who volunteer for an RCT. In contrast, we test managed charging with an experiment including all EVs within a California utility. Enrollment is low even with high incentives, and we can reject even modest intent-to-treat effects on electricity consumption. Managed charging is less effective than previously thought, underscoring the value of population-wide experiments.

title: Le Bureau des Légendes: A Dynamic Theory of Double Agents
affiliations: Department of Economics and

detail.title: Le Bureau des Légendes: A Dynamic Theory of Double Agents
detail.abstract:
This paper models double agents—individuals coerced into simultaneously serving two rival intelligence agencies—as a finite-horizon trilateral game between Agency A, Organization B, and the Mole M. The double agent persists within a corridor of survival: a set of bilateral beliefs under which both principals continue the relationship. Under a linear-quadratic-Gaussian benchmark, we obtain a closed-form characterization of the corridor geometry, analytical upper bounds on expected duration, and three main results: (i) existence of a double-agent equilibrium, (ii) structural transitoriness— belief updating, terminal unraveling, and compounding survival risk ensure inevitable collapse, and (iii) comparative statics linking monitoring technology, punishment severity, and protection costs to expected duration. The key mechanism is self-destructive experimentation: B learns about the mole’s type through both the type-dependence of effort and the traceability channel γ, which amplifies this learning. Extensions establish existence under general specifications and show that duration decays exponentially in the number of rival agencies. Predictions are consistent with historical patterns from Kim Philby to the Cold War mole hunts. The setting—bilateral coercion, existential participation constraints, and Bayesian learning in a finite-horizon trilateral structure— defines what we term antagonistic common agency.

title: The Unseen Costs of Blue Skies: Pollutant Substitution and Biodiversity Loss
affiliations: School of Global Policy and Strategy, Fudan University, East China Normal University (ECNU) and Shanghai International Studies University

detail.title: The Unseen Costs of Blue Skies: Pollutant Substitution and Biodiversity Loss
detail.abstract:
Incomplete performance metrics distort incentives. Exploiting the staggered roll-out of China’s national air monitoring network, we document a pollutant substitution effect: PM2.5 fell significantly, yet O3 surged. We trace this to strategic behavior: facing binding PM2.5 targets, local governments prioritized abatement of particulate precursors while neglecting ozone precursors. Critically, this was not a benign trade-off. Although the policy reduced PM2.5-attributed deaths, the policy-induced O3 surge increased O3-attributed mortality and reduced biodiversity (measured by bird abundance). Conservative estimates suggest these costs reduced the policy’s net benefits by approximately 23.8%. Our findings highlight the hidden social costs of narrow performance targeting.
